titulo: The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show, the ‘Super Bowl’ of Dog Shows

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: The lively schnauzer beat six other finalists in New York City to become the first of his breed to win Westminster’s “best in show.” The prize is the most important and respected in the U.S. dog show world.
While Monty came close to winning Westminster the past two years, he fell short of the big prize. In December 2024, the dog won another big prize, the huge American Kennel Club championship.

But for dog show lovers, Westminster is considered the Super Bowl of all shows. This year the comparison is especially fitting. That is because the most respected U.S. dog competition opened on the same weekend as the Super Bowl -- the most important game in American professional football. This rare happening came after the dates of both competitions changed in recent years.

At Westminster, dogs first compete against other members of their breed. Then, the winner of each breed goes up against other dogs within different competition “groups.” Among the groups are sporting, working, toy, and herding. Group winners then compete in the final round.
The best in show winner gets an award – a large, shiny cup called a trophy – and a place in dog-world history. The top prize, however, does not include money.

In her report on the dog show, Learning English’s Caty Weaver explains that the Westminster show dates back to 1877. It centers on the traditional purebred judging that leads to the best in show prize. But over the last few years, the organization has added agility and obedience events open to mixed-breed dogs.
And in 2023, a petit basset griffon Vendéen, named Buddy Holly, won best in show at Westminster. The breed he represents is known for its rabbit-hunting abilities.
titulo_es: La exposición canina del Westminster Kennel Club, la «Super Bowl» de los concursos de perros
resumen_es: Un schnauzer llamado Monty gana el premio «best in show» de Westminster, el concurso canino más prestigioso de Estados Unidos; el texto explica cómo funciona la competición y su historia.

ideas_clave.idea: Monty, a schnauzer, became the first dog of his breed to take Westminster's top award, after narrowly missing it in the two previous years and winning another major title in 2024.
Westminster is regarded as the Super Bowl of dog shows, and this year the two events even took place on the same weekend because their dates had shifted.
The contest has several stages: dogs compete first within their breed, then within groups, and the group winners meet in a final round.
The champion earns a trophy and a place in the history of the dog world, but no prize money.
The show, which goes back to 1877, focuses on traditional purebred judging but has recently opened agility and obedience events to mixed-breed dogs.
The 2023 winner was Buddy Holly, a petit basset griffon Vendéen, a breed known for hunting rabbits.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that Monty, a schnauzer, has won best in show at Westminster, the most prestigious dog show in the United States, becoming the first of his breed to do so after two near misses. Fittingly, the event, often called the Super Bowl of dog shows, coincided this year with the football final. Dogs compete first within their breed, then within groups, before a final round that brings a trophy but no money. Although rooted in purebred judging since 1877, the show now also welcomes mixed-breed dogs in some events.
